captureFeed.note: The row's blocker was a BINDING, not missing capability work: the probe proves the capability (eight graded legs, failures 0) but fed nothing into the full-harness report, so the grader could not credit the name. The probe's committed receipt is now a capture feed the repo's own grader (tools/edge-signed-in-exercise/lib/local-policy.mjs verifiedCapabilities) reads: fed the feed, this row grades covered with this one verified name and no other row moves. The feed cannot launder a red run - a red leg, a failure count, an unrecorded Ruby fact or another name all leave the row exactly where it was. The receipt's facts answer decko-ruby-reference/decko features/structure.feature:20-33 (create with plusses, see them in the main content, edit them in place, see them again, and the untouched default right keep its own content).

capabilities.finding: Bound to the name reference-harness/browser/probe-c13-create-and-edit-templated-card.mjs registers; before this binding the row declared no checks at all and could never be credited whatever a run did. That probe PASSED twice consecutively (.runtime/exhaustive/probe-C13/run1 and /run2: 8 of 8 graded legs GREEN in both, leg-by-leg verdicts identical, both runs exit 0) driving reference-harness/browser/engines/ts.json over reference-harness/fixtures/synthetic-v1 (fixtureSha256 066062bd09c25629d43691461a23bf37580e5cfe63cf68780fc4dfea2384f8aa) from a disposable pure-tip worktree at 9124c30d (sourceDiffSha256 e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855, the clean-tree value; distSha256 c8d6e53c396d9695c07467f1c7225a36ed64670f3663bf820613bd7c2455fb91 recomputed from that worktree's own dist/ and equal to its build record). What it measured: the fixture (a Cardtype whose structure rule adds a templated right carrying a *right+*default rule) is seeded through the engine's own create endpoint and read back out of the deck - rule rows in this port are junction-shaped (name and key NULL, left_id/right_id set), so they are read by walking left_id, never by name; GET /new/<Cardtype> serves card[type_id] equal to the seeded Cardtype's id (the assertion lib/typed-fixture.mjs:41 makes, guarding the silent-substitution bug broken-things-for-the-report-2026-10-18.md records) and the templated subcard editor arrives PRE-FILLED, read through the live TinyMCE instance rather than a hidden carrier; the card is then created by one Submit with the nested editor never typed into, so the stored junction row's content came from the server; /<card>?view=edit edits that subcard and the stock Save and Close control (<button type=submit data-cy=submit-modal class="... _close-on-success ...">Save and Close</button> - this engine does NOT use a data-cy=save-and-close button, and the receipt names the control it clicked) answers 200 on /update/<card>, closes the modal, and BOTH the stored junction row and a fresh GET carry the new text. Four controls keep those legs non-vacuous: a second, non-templated right in the SAME structure rule renders an empty editor (so the pre-fill is attributable to the *right+*default rule rather than to a constant); the nested junction row holds the template BEFORE the edit; the create submit is required to go through the graded fixture's own form (a submit driven from another create page stores a card of that page's type and no nested row - the first run of the isolation observation below caught exactly that, which is why CONTROL-C exists); and the signed-in session survives the whole drive. STATUS DELIBERATELY STAYS not_covered: the grading rule (lib/local-policy.mjs:47-55) credits a name only against result.check in a full-harness run, and this check is registered by the reference-harness probe, which does not feed that report - fed the probe's own results the repo's verifiedCapabilities computes covered for this row (verified at binding time, both runs), and with no results it computes not_covered, so declaring covered here would claim more than the registry's own rule can check. Measured while binding, and worth knowing before another templated fixture is written: on this engine GET /new/<Cardtype> is fed by the <Cardtype>+*type+*structure rule. The design names <Cardtype>+*self+*structure, and that rule form alone served ZERO nested content fields on both runs (the probe's recorded, not graded, C13-OBSERVED-STRUCTURE-RULE-VARIANT leg seeds a second Cardtype carrying only the self rule over the same two rights and reads its create form; a four-way seed sweep behind that observation is preserved at .runtime/exhaustive/probe-C13/seed-sweep/). Both rule forms are therefore seeded and LEG-1 does not depend on which one applied.

capabilities.capability: Upload a file (/files route after upload)
capabilities.note: the live edge environment carries no DECKO_STORAGE_* variables; expected to fail on the edge, to be confirmed
checks: F1 a file can be uploaded through the File create form
F1 the uploaded card offers the /files route as a Download link
capabilities.finding: COVERED, and the finding this row carried for six tranches was wrong. The old finding said '/new/File has no file input; the generic new-card form has no file branch', and the tranche-8 receipt repeated it as a port gap. THE PORT WAS NEVER THE GAP. The /new/File page is the mod-composed new form (the engine's own comment at deploy/bunny-worker-src/bunny-edge-engine-request.ts:1076-1080 says so: File/Image dispatch carrierwave's chooser), and the port's chooser bytes are byte for byte the committed real-Ruby capture's: reference-harness/fixtures/synthetic-v2-mod-probes/expected/render.jsonl, arm probe-view:98:input@set/type/file.rb, reads `<input class='file-upload slotter form-control' id='card_file' name='card[file]' type='file'>` and `<input class="attachment_card_name form-control" value="" autocomplete="off" type="hidden" name="card[file]" id="card_file" />`, and src/card/mod-loader/mods/card-mod-carrierwave.ts:536-556 renders the same bytes. The F1 upload leg has always passed. WHAT THE LEG ACTUALLY GRADED WRONGLY, and both halves were the CHECK's, not the port's. (1) The hidden carrier was matched against the HAML's literal `class: "attachment_card_name"` instead of the class TOKEN, and the rendered class carries decko's bootstrap form class as well (card-mod-bootstrap's form component adds it to every field), so a field the port renders byte for byte read as absent. (2) The chip was read off the SAVED card's page, where no chip can be in either system: the chip is preview_editor.haml's bytes, and Ruby renders that view ONLY inside the two-step upload's round trip - outside it the view RAISES, because preview_editor.haml line 2 calls cached_upload_card_name and Card::Env.params[:attachment_upload] is nil. The same capture says so verbatim: arm probe-view:100:preview_editor@set/type/file.rb is 'undefined method gsub for nil' at set/type/file.rb:145. So the chip rides the round trip's RESPONSE, which the browser swaps into the form's .chosen-file (upload.js.coffee:48-51), and the saved card's page carries core.haml and nothing else. The leg now waits for the round trip (the draft id in the preview's hidden input) and reads the chip out of the FORM, while the download anchor is still read out of the saved card's page. MEASURED: the whole-family exercise at source 237991861, 252 of 253 checks passed, both F1 legs PASS (the /files route's anchor href /files/~53155/154.txt, and the chip {filename: harness.txt, size: 17 Bytes}), and the family's own grader reads F1 covered - 70 covered, 20 partial, 1 not covered, 3 out of scope of 95. The one remaining red in that run is the engine's own 3 s server-time budget, not this row. The row's own note about the edge carrying no DECKO_STORAGE_* variables is untouched.

capabilities.capability: Unfollow from the board
capabilities.finding: Left not_covered: no id-prefixed check ran for this row in recorded run strengthened-full-harness-52fc9b7e (completedAt 2026-10-19T00:21:57.951Z, 242 results, 242 pass) (the run's only unfollow result is W6's mail-link check, a different surface). The board unfollow leg is evidenced outside the harness, so this row needs a probe, not a binding. [2026-10-20 capability-inventory tranche 4] THE UNFOLLOW HALF, GRADED ON FOUR BYTES AND THE STORED RULE. The row is right that a binding would not have closed it and that this needs an instrument: the run's only unfollow result was W6, which is a DIFFERENT SURFACE - the unfollow link inside the follower MAIL (card-mod-follow set/all/notify/base_views.rb:48-55 view :unfollow_url, built by follow-mail-views.ts:252-258). W2 is the unfollow control on the board's Engage tab. Two surfaces, two byte contracts, and conflating them is how W2 stayed uncovered while W6 went green. WHAT WAS GRADED BEFORE: W1 (checks-cover-b.mjs:1115-1116) reads linksAfter.some(t => /^following$/i.test(t)) - the LINK TEXT and nothing else. Ruby's two link states differ on FOUR independent values (start_follow_link.rb:4-11 vs stop_follow_link.rb:4-11): rule_content *always/*never, link_text follow/following, action send/stop sending, css_class empty/btn-item-delete, plus hover_text unfollow on the stop state only, with follow_link.rb:44-69 supplying link_opts, the action-emails-about-changes title, the follow-verb span and the path's card: {content: [[rule_content]]}. follow_link_views.rb:3-5 picks the class BY STATE (card.followed? ? StopFollowLink : StartFollowLink). So an anchor that says following while its href still writes *always passes W1 and is broken: clicking it would RE-follow the card. All four bytes are now graded per state, read out of the anchor itself. THE STORAGE ROUND TRIP, WHICH NOTHING GRADED: the path's card: {content: ...} is a WRITE, and whether it took is a separate question from how the link renders. The stored preference is read from the deck through the rule card (set/right/following.rb current_follow_rule_card -> card.left.preference :follow), never inferred from the page. A link that says following over a stored *never is a card that will never mail described as one that will - that inversion is invisible to every byte-level leg, and it is the defect class this row is about. A third leg exists because the follower_ids set is CACHED (follower_ids.rb FOLLOWER_IDS_CACHE_KEY, write/read_follower_ids_cache): a stop that removed the rule but left the cache renders *never in storage while still counting the former follower, and follow_section.rb:31-36 renders that count as the followers link's own label, so the count is the only leg that sees it. Four legs, graded apart: the start link, the stop link, the storage, and the revert (which re-checks the start bytes AND the count baseline). tools/edge-signed-in-exercise/lib/unfollow-from-board.mjs holds the predicate; checks-cover-b.mjs drives the transition as the member on a card it created. The port already emits both states byte for byte (src/card/mod-loader/mods/card-mod-edit.ts:3640-3671 followButton), so by parity law the RENDERING is not what this commit repairs; what was never driven is the transition. STATUS UNCHANGED, and deliberately: the row stays not_covered and the four legs are its FIRST declared checks - the row had none, which is why the grader could only say not_covered. Four declared checks that have never run grade as not_covered under the repo instrument (lib/local-policy.mjs:44-57: passed.length is zero, so the declared status is irrelevant), and promoting the row to partial would claim credit that does not exist. Declaring the legs is not passing them; grading them needs a signed-in deck run, which this tranche does not have.

[2026-10-21 signed-in battery] THE SIGNED-IN LEG RAN AND THE CREATE IS WHERE IT FAILS. The same full run (committed record docs/runs/edge-signed-in-exercise-full-run-2026-10-21-tranche5-signed-in-leg.md, 263/292 checks passing at source 698faa29, completed 2026-10-21T17:47:53Z) passed the form leg (the anonymous GET of /new/Sign_up rendered Ruby's own field set, action and success mark) and then refused the anonymous sign-up itself: POST /card/create answered 422 and re-rendered the bare sign-up form with no error content (run capture 070-account-signup-success, htmlSha256 6c769323a628ed781c13273632b7b4db17aa4955dc86a459a8a73a007d3a13d1), one request after the module's Background setup completed (its single create answered 303 in the run's request ledger, immediately before the anonymous form GET). [2026-10-21 capability-inventory afix] THE CREATE ARM MATCHES RUBY, AND THE LEG RAN GREEN. Three named defects stood between the port and the flow, each fixed on its own evidence: (1) THE NAME NEVER REACHED THE CREATE - the anonymous /new/:type arm rendered the name prompt unconditionally, so the form posted an empty card[name] and the engine refused 422 name-illegal; the route now reads card[name] off the query and renders Ruby's NAMED shape, the one the committed real-Ruby capture carries (hide [name_formgroup], the hidden card[name] field), and the check's Background runs as the administrator the way signup.feature's does (the anonymous rule write was refused 403, so the scenario's permission never existed).
